hypothesis: A near-expiry sub-strategy (enter only Monday 13:00-15:20, 1 day before Tuesday expiry) will produce dramatically higher average P&L per trade (>₹2,000) than the unfiltered baseline (₹77).
notes: EXP-0002 FINDING-1: 15 Monday-afternoon 1-day-out trades generated ₹42k (avg ₹2,803). Remaining 64 March trades = ₹-1.6k combined. Test this as a standalone sub-strategy. Key risk: very low trade frequency (3-4 per month). Need at least 30 trades for valid stats → will need longer backtest period beyond Feb-Jul 2026.
conclusion: HYPOTHESIS REJECTED (as standalone sub-strategy). Only 13 qualifying trades in 6 months — far below the 30-trade minimum for statistical significance. However, avg P&L/trade (₹422) is 3x baseline (₹141), confirming the quality is there. RECOMMENDATION: Do not use as standalone strategy due to insufficient frequency. Instead, use near-expiry status as a POSITION SIZING SIGNAL — increase lots by 2-3x when days_to_expiry=1 and session is AFTERNOON. Needs much longer data history (12+ months) for proper validation.
